gloss: to read the room, to pick up on the atmosphere

definitions.gloss: to read the room, to pick up on the atmosphere
definitions.explanation: To sense the mood or unspoken feelings of those around you and act appropriately. A key social skill in Japanese culture.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{空気|くうき}を{読|よ}むのが{上手|じょうず}だ。
examples.english: He's good at reading the room.

examples.japanese: {会議中|かいぎちゅう}に{空気|くうき}を{読|よ}まずに{冗談|じょうだん}を{言|い}って、{場|ば}が{凍|こお}った。
examples.english: I told a joke without reading the room during the meeting, and everyone went silent.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
Reading the air ({空気|くうき}を{読|よ}む) is considered a fundamental social skill in Japan. Someone who fails to do this is called KY ({空気|くうき}{読|よ}めない, unable to read the room), which became a popular slang abbreviation.

The particle を is sometimes dropped in casual speech: {空気|くうき}{読|よ}んで instead of {空気|くうき}を{読|よ}んで.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {空気|くうき}を{読|よ}む: to read the room
- {空気|くうき}が{読|よ}める: to be able to read the room
- {空気|くうき}が{読|よ}めない (KY): unable to read the room
- {場|ば}の{空気|くうき}を{読|よ}む: to read the atmosphere of the situation
